statement: Combine up to six scheme types (user preferences, company standards, shortcuts, tools, command layout, workspace) into named work-environment profiles that can be applied, set as default, exported and imported.
superiority: Profiles are JSON and shareable by team via a cloud library.
notes: CORRECTED — read Work Environment Profiles and Work Environment Schemes; profiles only reference schemes; a locked icon marks read-only items; profiles and schemes exchange as XML. Acceptance sketch: Switch profile: toolbar set and shortcuts change accordingly and persist after restart.

statement: Assign keyboard shortcuts to commands and functions per window type, warn on collisions and allow reassigning, within shortcut schemes that can be exported.
superiority: Chord and multi-key shortcuts as well as command-line aliases.
notes: CORRECTED — read Shortcut Customization Dialog Box and Shortcuts; collision shown as 'currently assigned to', Assign anyway detaches the earlier command; shortcut lists for favourites were not found. Acceptance sketch: Assign Ctrl+Alt+K to a command and trigger it; a conflicting assignment is flagged.

statement: Search for commands by name from a global search.
superiority: Natural-language command search.
notes: REJECTED: no help page documents a global command search or Find Command field in Archicad 30 (searched 'find command', 'search commands'); the only command search is the list filter in the shortcut and menu customisation dialogs. Acceptance sketch: Search finds command by partial name.

statement: Save work to a recovery file at a chosen interval or after each step, keep a backup copy of the previous save, and offer to resume interrupted work after a crash.
superiority: Continuous journaling gives zero data loss.
notes: CORRECTED — read Data Safety & Integrity; recovery modes Ultra Safe, Safe (5 min), Minimum (20 min); Make Backup Copy writes a .bpn; Backup Files page explains opening it; library parts and render images are not covered. Acceptance sketch: Killing the process leaves an autosave with at most one interval of lost work that reopens.

statement: Multiple language user interfaces and localised libraries.

source.ref: Platform: Localised versions and language switching

superiority: Runtime language switching.
notes: UNVERIFIED — the help mentions 'localized version' only in passing (shortcuts, commands not available in every localization); no help page documents UI language switching or localised library handling. Acceptance sketch: Language change applies after restart.

statement: Keyboard reach of all dialog controls and screen reader labels.
superiority: Audited against WCAG 2.2 AA.
notes: REJECTED: no Archicad 30 help page documents screen-reader labels or full keyboard reach of dialog controls (searched accessibility, screen reader); only keyboard navigation inside tool settings panels is described. Acceptance sketch: Tab order reaches every control and each has an accessible name.

statement: Customise the content and order of menus and store the command layout, including toolbars, as a command layout scheme in the work environment.
superiority: Menu layout is a data file merged by rules, so updates never clobber user changes.
notes: CORRECTED — read Menu Customization Dialog Box and Menus; any command can be placed in any menu except context menus; the Quick Options Bar content is not documented as customisable. Acceptance sketch: Move a command to a new menu: it shows there after restart and the default layout can be restored.

statement: Choose Tracker display (always or on demand), show Z and parameter tags, prefer polar or Cartesian coordinates, show values relative to the user origin, and set Tracker colours and transparency.
superiority: Same input grammar as the command line used everywhere.
notes: CORRECTED — read Tracker and Coordinate Input and Tracker; the Control Box holds drawing aids, not coordinates (see UI-0020); input shortcuts X/Y/Z/D/A are in the Tracker topic. Acceptance sketch: Typing polar 3 at 30 degrees places a point at (2.598, 1.5) within 1e-9.

statement: Search commands by name from a global search field and run them.
superiority: Natural-language command search with usage hints.
notes: REJECTED: duplicate of UI-0003; no global command search found in Archicad 30 help. Acceptance sketch: Searching a partial name lists the matching commands and runs the selected one.

statement: Transfer a selection between the floor plan, section and 3D windows with context commands that select it in the other window or show only it in 3D, using tabs for open windows.
superiority: Selection sync across all windows and the schedule.
notes: CORRECTED — read Special Selection Commands and Tab Bar; windows are tabs, not tiles; no automatic simultaneous highlighting across tiled windows is documented. Acceptance sketch: Select a wall in plan: the same GUID is highlighted in 3D and section.

statement: Zoom to the selection, step back and forward through the last twenty zoom values, and store named or home zooms, optionally across stories.
superiority: Navigation bookmarks and saved view stack.
notes: CORRECTED — read Zoom; Previous/Next Zoom keep up to 20 zooms; Set Home Zoom saved with project; named zooms saved per story or across all stories and applied from View Settings. Acceptance sketch: Zoom to selection frames the element bounding box with the set margin.

statement: Show pet palette commands that depend on the selected element, on whether an edge, node or surface is hit, and on the window type, with a user choice of whether the palette follows the cursor.
superiority: Context menu generated from the command registry.
notes: VERIFIED — read Pet Palettes and Menus; pet palette contents are not customisable; context menus are not customisable; palette movement set in Dialog Boxes and Palettes. Acceptance sketch: Right-click a wall lists wall-specific commands.

statement: Provide 3D display options such as hardware-acceleration effects, a software fallback and navigation smoothness controlled by a frames-per-second target and a minimum radius of always-shown elements.
superiority: Automatic level-of-detail tuning.
notes: CORRECTED — read Hardware Acceleration Options (via 3D Styles) and Navigation in the 3D Window; cache size or GPU selection controls were not found. Acceptance sketch: Changing quality changes frame rate measurably on a reference model.

statement: Native builds on Apple silicon and Windows with the same feature set.

source.ref: Platform: native Apple silicon and Windows builds

superiority: One codebase and identical results.
notes: UNVERIFIED — help shows separate Intel-based Mac and Windows installers in the BIM manager guide only; no help page discusses Apple silicon builds or feature parity; this is a packaging fact, not an editor feature. Acceptance sketch: A reference project opens and produces identical geometry hashes on both.

statement: Multiple UI languages and localised libraries and templates.
superiority: Runtime language switching without restart.
notes: UNVERIFIED — duplicate of UI-0005; only incidental mentions of localised versions in help; no page on localised libraries, templates or language switching was found. Acceptance sketch: Switching language relabels all dialogs and keeps project data unchanged.

statement: Set length, area, volume, angle and layout units with decimal places or fractions for the project, with separate units for dimensioning.
superiority: Mixed units accepted per field.
notes: CORRECTED — read Working Units; also covers surveyor's unit, numbers without units; dimension units are in Dimensions Preferences, not in Working Units. Acceptance sketch: Switching units changes displays and not the stored geometry.

statement: Customise which panels appear in each tool's Info Box and in what order, with show/hide per panel, and store the result as a tool scheme.
superiority: Let every palette and panel be arranged freely with per-document and per-user overrides, saved as shareable JSON.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Info Box Customization Dialog Box and Info Box; header texts can be hidden; Info Box shows selected/editable counts. Acceptance sketch: Hide the Layer panel of the wall tool: Info Box for walls omits it, other tools unchanged; restore via the tool scheme.

statement: Create and edit custom toolbars of commands and menus, choosing icon, name or both per command, stored as part of a command layout scheme.
superiority: Let toolbars hold macros and scripted commands and sync between devices.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Toolbar Customization Dialog Box and Toolbars; menus can be added to toolbars with sticky pop-up behaviour; on-screen toolbar display saved in workspace scheme. Acceptance sketch: Create toolbar 'X' with two commands and icon-only mode: toolbar shows two icons and persists after restart via its scheme.

statement: Offer a Quick Options Bar showing the active window's zoom, orientation, layer combination, scale, pen set, view option combinations, renovation filter, 3D style and similar settings for quick switching.
superiority: Make the bar fully user-configurable and context-aware per window type.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Quick Options Bar; it can also be shown as a palette; some entries are not available in the layout or 3D windows. Acceptance sketch: Change scale in the bar to 1:50: the active window's scale becomes 1:50 and the dialog for that setting opens on request.

statement: Provide a Control Box palette with OK/Cancel for the current operation and icons for guide lines, relative construction methods (parallel, perpendicular, angle bisector, offset, snap-point vector, align to surface) and gravity.
superiority: Show only the constraints that apply to the current tool and let them be triggered by keys as well as icons.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Control Box; not visible by default; horizontal/vertical or compact/extended forms; relative construction methods listed in the pop-up. Acceptance sketch: Choose Perpendicular, click a reference edge, then draw a wall: new wall direction is exactly perpendicular to that edge.

statement: Explore the model in a perspective view with mouse look, W-A-S-D or arrow-key walking, a fly mode, lift keys and speed control, without editing while active.
superiority: Support smooth first-person navigation on any view type with collision-aware walking.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Explore Model (3D Navigation); only in perspective views, F toggles Fly, PageUp/Space and PageDown/C lift; optimised for hardware acceleration engine. Acceptance sketch: In Explore mode pressing W moves the camera along its view direction on the horizontal plane; pressing Esc restores edit mode.

statement: Orbit the 3D model around its centre or target point by dragging, with a temporary orbit via Shift plus the scroll button while editing.
superiority: Keep orbit centre selectable (pick-point or selection) and allow editing while orbiting.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Orbit (3D Navigation); no editing while orbit mode is active; temporary Shift+wheel orbit works in edit mode but requires redraw. Acceptance sketch: Dragging 90 pixels horizontally rotates the model by the configured angle about its centre point; Esc returns to edit mode.

statement: Set colours, bold contours, transparency and delay of selection dots, selection and pre-selection highlights and associated-element highlights used while selecting and inputting elements.
superiority: Provide accessible high-contrast presets and per-theme highlight sets.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Selection and Element Information and Selection Highlights; element information tags can reuse Tracker colours. Acceptance sketch: Set highlight delay to 0.5 s: hovering a selectable element shows its highlight after 0.5 s, or immediately with Shift.
